body:
Problem:
`g@<C-v>j` and `y<C-v>j` set '] one char short of the block corner, so
'operatorfunc' cannot get the block. With 'virtualedit' "block", "y"
also yanks a short last line one column narrow.

Solution:
- Decide `inclusive` from the motion's own type, before get_op_vcol()
  makes it blockwise (like Vim).
- Never exclude the end of a block from '] (`g@<C-v>l`): a block
  includes its corner.


Fixes neovim/neovim#42309

comment_data.body:
Small suggestion: this comment explains a line that is not there anymore. A new reader does not know that `motion_type` was set here before, so "stays" is hard to understand. `kMTBlockWise` is now set next to the `'V'` and `'v'` cases, and the test covers the order, so I think the comment can go.

```suggestion
```

```
it('forced-blockwise motion (o_CTRL-V): g@ and y get the block #42309', function()
  local marks = [=[[getpos("'[")[1:3], getpos("']")[1:3]]]=]
  n.exec(([[
    func! Op(type) abort
      let g:op = [a:type] + %s
    endfunc
    set operatorfunc=Op
  ]]):format(marks))
  --- Asserts that g@ and y see the same block: '[ and '] marks, and the yanked text.
  local function assert_block(lines, keys, expected_marks, expected_text)
    api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, true, lines)
    feed(keys)
    eq({ 'block', unpack(expected_marks) }, api.nvim_get_var('op'), keys)
    feed((keys:gsub('g@', 'y')))
    eq(expected_marks, n.eval(marks), keys)
    eq(expected_text, fn.getreg('"', 1, 1), keys)
  end
  assert_block({ 'seed', 'ab', 'cd' }, '2G0g@<C-v>j', { { 2, 1, 0 }, { 3, 1, 0 } }, { 'a', 'c' })
  assert_block({ 'seed', 'ab', 'cd' }, '2G0g@<C-v>e', { { 2, 1, 0 }, { 2, 2, 0 } }, { 'ab' })
  -- Exclusive motion: the block still includes the end.
  assert_block({ 'abcd' }, '02|g@<C-v>l', { { 1, 2, 0 }, { 1, 3, 0 } }, { 'bc' })
  command('set selection=exclusive')
  assert_block({ 'abcd' }, '02|g@<C-v>l', { { 1, 2, 0 }, { 1, 2, 0 } }, { 'b' })
  command('set selection&')
  -- Short last line: '] keeps the right edge (past EOL).
  command('set virtualedit=block')
  assert_block(
    { 'abcdef', 'abcdef', 'ab' },
    '1G4|g@<C-v>2j',
    { { 1, 2, 0 }, { 3, 3, 1 } },
    { 'bcd', 'bcd', 'b  ' }
  )
  -- "d" deletes the block, not the lines.
  api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, true, { 'ab', 'cd' })
  feed('gg0d<C-v>j')
  eq({ 'b', 'd' }, api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, 0, -1, true))
end)
```

comment_regular_data.body:
Thanks for this PR. It fixes the linewise case (`<C-v>j`). But the exclusive case (row 3 in #42309) is not fixed:

```
:call setline(1, ['ab cd'])
0y<C-v>w
```

The register is correct (`ab c`). But `']` is at column 3. It must be at column 4. With `selection=exclusive`, `02|y<C-v>l` puts `']` before `'[`.

The cause: `op_function()` and `op_yank_reg()` do `decl()` on blocks too. For a block, `oap->end` is already the last column.

I have a fix with a test: https://github.com/Nagato-Yuzuru/neovim/commit/c4592655339c6d43b799f1f5b65f2f4fe912fedb

It changes only these two conditions. It applies cleanly on this branch:

```bash
git fetch https://github.com/Nagato-Yuzuru/neovim fix-forced-block-exclusive
git cherry-pick c4592655339c
```

You can add it to this PR. Or I can send a separate PR after this PR is merged.
Thanks for catching this and providing the fix! I’ve cherry-picked your commit and removed the outdated comment in get_op_vcol(). Really appreciate your help!

Thanks for the review.

Three updates are in this PR:

1. A forced blockwise exclusive motion such as `g@<C-v>l` no longer leaves `']` one character short. `']` stays on the corner of the block. This is the change from Nagato-Yuzuru.
2. The comment in `get_op_vcol()` is removed. It described an assignment that is no longer in that function.
3. The operator test is now the single example you posted. It runs each motion once with `g@` and once with `y`, and checks that both see the same block.

The failing checks are not from this PR. All of them fail `has() "patch-x.y.z"`: `has('patch-8.2.0')` returns 1, and `test/functional/vimscript/has_spec.lua` still expects 0. CI merges this branch with current master, and 0247e5fd adds patch 0 to the Vim 8.2 list in `src/nvim/version.c`. This PR does not change that file. In those logs, `operator_spec.lua` passed.

Glad to make a contribution to Nvim!
Please rebase, the failing test should be fixed now

> 1. A forced blockwise exclusive motion such as `g@<C-v>l` no longer leaves `']` one character short. `']` stays on the corner of the block. This is the change from Nagato-Yuzuru.

@Icyjerry, @Nagato-Yuzuru, could you please elaborate on the reasoning about why exclusive motion is forced to be inclusive here? In particular, why this change *had to* be made instead of adjusting this in user/plugin code?

The `:h exclusive` describe the previous behavior pretty explicitly:

> Character motion is either inclusive or exclusive.  When inclusive, the start and end position of the motion are included in the operation. When exclusive, the last character towards the end of the buffer is not included.

This PR make it not the case for forced blockwise selection with an exclusive motion (like `` `a ``, as described in `:h mark-motions`). I don't think this is a *huge* deal, but it is not great to break backward compatibility for something that (I think) might be accounted on the user side and is documented.

I went back and tested my original patch, and it seems it already fixes the reported issue without changing the exclusive-motion behavior.

The problem was that g@<C-v>j is linewise, but the motion was marked blockwise before inclusive was determined, so it ended up being treated as exclusive. Using the original motion type fixes the wrong '] position and the missing column on short lines, while still matching Vim.

The later change skips decl() for all block motions, mainly to let 'operatorfunc' get the full block from '[ and ']. But this also changes how exclusive motions work, which wasn’t needed for the original issue.

I didn’t really think about how this could affect plugins depending on the old behavior. Thanks for pointing it out! I agree it’s better to keep the existing behavior here. I’m happy to revert that extra part and keep my original fix.

> I didn’t really think about how this could affect plugins depending on the old behavior. Thanks for pointing it out! I agree it’s better to keep the existing behavior here. I’m happy to revert that extra part and keep my original fix.

I *think* that if it can be reverted while fixing the known issues and still show the intended Vim behavior, then it is a good thing to do to avoid an unnecessary breaking change.

To elaborate, what *exactly* changed is the application of custom operator on forced blockwise selection after `` ` `` jump. Like `` g@<C-v>`a `` showed one behavior, but after this PR it acted as if `a` mark was placed one more column to the right.

Thanks! I’ve opened a follow-up PR (#42350) to restore the previous exclusive-motion behavior while keeping the original fix.

g@<C-v>`a is now exclusive again, with '] one column before the mark, matching Vim and 0.12. The fixes for g@<C-v>j and short-line yanks are preserved.

@echasnovski  Let me explain. Thank you for the careful review.

> after this PR it acted as if `a` mark was placed one more column to the right.

Yes, `']` moves one column to the right. This is the intended fix. Now `g@` gets the same block as `y` and `d`:

| ``<C-v>`a``, `'a` at 2:2 on `abcd` / `efgh` | `']` | `getregion("'[", "']")` | ``y<C-v>`a`` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2f047b5668` (before this PR) | 2:1 | `a`, `e` | `ab`, `ef` |
| `c459265533` (this PR) | 2:2 | `ab`, `ef` | `ab`, `ef` |

> The `:h exclusive` describe the previous behavior pretty explicitly

`:h exclusive` describes what the operation includes. With `<C-v>`, the operation always includes the end column: `y` and `d` did this before this PR, as `:h o_CTRL-V` says. Only `']` did not agree with the operation, because `decl()` excluded the end after `oap->end` was already the last column of the block. `:h ']` and `:h g@` put `']` on "the last character of the text". Thus the old `']` was not documented behavior. It was a bug.

Without `<C-v>`, nothing changes: ``g@`a`` and ``y`a`` give the same result as before.

> why this change *had to* be made instead of adjusting this in user/plugin code?

Plugin code cannot know the correct block. An operatorfunc gets only `"block"`, not the motion. Before this PR, `<C-v>l` and `<C-v>tb` from `a` on `abcd` both gave `'[` = `']` = 1:1, but the blocks are `ab` and `a`. Before #42119, an operatorfunc could get the block from `'<`/`'>`. Now `'[`/`']` are the only source.

> if it can be reverted while fixing the known issues and still show the intended Vim behavior

The exclusive case is one of the known issues. It is in #42309 (row 4: `g@<C-v>l` gives one column, `y<C-v>l` yanks two). The fix for `<C-v>j` alone does not fix it.

Vim has the same bug, and I reported it: vim/vim#21511. Thus I think the old `']` is not intended Vim behavior.

> > The `:h exclusive` describe the previous behavior pretty explicitly
> 
> `:h exclusive` describes what the operation includes. With `<C-v>`, the operation always includes the end column: `y` and `d` did this before this PR, as `:h o_CTRL-V` says.

Reading the `:h o_CTRL-V` I am still not convinced that that new behavior is the intended one. There is nothing about making the blockwise region exclusive. The only relevant part is `This works like Visual block mode selection, with the corners defined by the cursor position before and after the motion.`. The only thing here is that it makes regular motion be treated like block and not charwise/linewise. There is no assumption that it *also* forces the region to be inclusive.

Contrast it to `:h o_v` note: `If the motion already was charwise, toggle exclusive.  This can be used to make an exclusive motion inclusive and an inclusive motion exclusive.`.

How operators, including built-in ones, decide to deal with provided region data is up to operators. If `y` and `d` (and others, I tested `gU` for more visual clarity) decide to treat it as inclusive, that's their decision.

> Plugin code cannot know the correct block. An operatorfunc gets only `"block"`, not the motion. Before this PR, `<C-v>l` and `<C-v>tb` from `a` on `abcd` both gave `'[` = `']` = 1:1, but the blocks are `ab` and `a`. Before #42119, an operatorfunc could get the block from `'<`/`'>`. Now `'[`/`']` are the only source.

This still fits the docs and feels like intended:
- `l` is exclusive motion (`dl` deletes only character under cursor). So the block is only `a`.
- `t` is inclusive motion. So the block is also `a`.

---

After (trying to) read to docs, it feels like `<C-v>` forcing *also* inclusive region with built-in operators is something that doesn't fit the docs. But I guess reverting *that* behavior is more problematic than adjusting the `g@` behavior. And making them align with each other indeed sounds like a good idea.

Thanks for the discussion! Aligning g@ with y and d makes sense, and the merged code already does that.

I opened #42350 following our earlier discussion about restoring the old '] position. I’ve marked it as draft for now and will leave the merged behavior as it is.

Thank you, I agree the docs do not cover this. In practice, a forced block follows Visual block mode: `'selection'` decides if the end column is included, not the motion (with `selection=exclusive`, `y<C-v>l` yanks one column and `y<C-v>e` yanks two).

I will send a docs PR for `:h o_CTRL-V` and `news.txt`, and the same change to Vim (vim/vim#21511).
